section_summary: This section covers post-election party realignment in Japan, including Democratic Party strategy and the Social Democratic Party’s shift to the left. It also contains Ichirō Hatoyama’s lengthy appeal against his purge, a Soviet protest against the purge of Jiichirō Matsumoto, and correspondence about political polarization and foreign investment. Several items are enclosures or duplicate filing copies.

subfiles.title: Democratic Party realignment after the January election
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports Kojima Tetsuzō’s assessment of party realignment, election tactics, communism, and the Democratic Party’s future.
subfiles.summary: Kojima describes Democratic Liberal support for candidates opposed to Ashida faction Democrats and credits Communist gains partly to tax campaigning. He urges the Democrats to remain outside government, cooperate with Socialists, and build local organization; the despatch considers a possible center-left realignment while noting weak leadership and corruption.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of conversation with Kojima Tetsuzō
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser’s office, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Records Kojima’s views on coalition politics, elections, SCAP policy, and a possible Democratic-Socialist alignment.
subfiles.summary: Kojima recounts the struggle between the Ashida and Inukai factions, Democratic Liberal election assistance to Inukai allies, and Communist use of tax grievances. He argues that SCAP should take public responsibility for its policies or allow more Japanese discretion. He favors single-member constituencies and predicts further Communist gains. For the Democrats, he recommends opposition, stronger local organization, cooperation with Socialists, and eventual union with their right wing.

subfiles.title: Cover letter transmitting January report from Japan
subfiles.from: Leonard Jacob II, International Telephone and Telegraph Corporation
subfiles.about: Transmits excerpts from monthly reports by overseas subsidiaries and associated companies.
subfiles.summary: Sends monthly report excerpts for possible State Department interest.

subfiles.title: January 1949 report from Japan: political situation
subfiles.from: International Telephone and Telegraph Corporation subsidiary or associated company in Japan
subfiles.about: Summarizes election results and SCAP decisions on foreign investment and stock exchanges.
subfiles.summary: The report records the Democratic Liberal landslide, Communist gains, and losses by coalition parties in the January 23 election. It describes new rules allowing limited foreign business activity and investment, the Foreign Investment Board, and approval to reopen controlled securities exchanges.

subfiles.title: Bishop letter on Japan’s party system
subfiles.about: Questions whether Japan should have one broad non-socialist party and asks Sebald’s views.
subfiles.summary: Bishop favors a choice between two non-Communist parties and asks Sebald to clarify earlier analysis.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Hatoyama petition for rescreening
subfiles.about: Forwards Hatoyama Ichirō’s second appeal against his political purge.
subfiles.summary: Explains why Hatoyama addressed this appeal directly to MacArthur.

subfiles.title: Second petition for rescreening of my political purge
subfiles.about: Seeks reversal of Hatoyama’s political purge through rebuttals, recollections, and letters offered as evidence.
subfiles.summary: Hatoyama disputes each stated basis for his purge, including actions as cabinet secretary and education minister, his writings, and his 1942 election address. He portrays himself as a liberal parliamentarian who opposed militarism, wartime controls, the Imperial Rule Assistance movement, and war with Britain and the United States. He recounts political disputes and attempts to change wartime leadership, then reproduces friends’ letters to support his account. He asks MacArthur to review both petitions and release him from the purge.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Present Conditions of Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards copies of a Japanese Foreign Office pamphlet on current conditions.
subfiles.summary: Sends five copies of Present Conditions of Japan and notes its official perspective.

subfiles.title: State Department inquiry about Kades’s purge remarks
subfiles.about: Requests clarification of reported Kades remarks and adherence to established purge policy.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether Kades made the reported remarks and what action the Army proposes.

subfiles.title: Nippon Times article on Kades and the election
subfiles.doc_type: newspaper clipping fragment, with blank following page
subfiles.about: Reports Kades’s comments on SCAP authority, purge policy, and Japan’s election results.
subfiles.summary: Kades describes SCAP’s authority and attributes the election result to reaction against incumbent parties and the Shōwa Denkō scandal.

subfiles.title: The Social Democratic Party’s Shift to the Left
subfiles.about: Assesses the Social Democratic Party’s leftward reorganization at its March 1949 convention.
subfiles.summary: The convention elected Suzuki Mosaburō secretary general, strengthened labor representation, and adopted changes to party organization while declining a Marxist platform. The despatch considers whether the party can attract labor support and resist Communist influence. It also describes weaker right wing leadership, Hirano Rikizō’s purge, and the political costs of the earlier coalition cabinets.

subfiles.title: Soviet protest against purge of Matsumoto Jiichirō
subfiles.about: Forwards a Soviet Allied Council member’s protest against Matsumoto’s disqualification.
subfiles.summary: The adviser reports broad Japanese criticism of Matsumoto’s purge and observes that Soviet and Communist support has become prominent.

subfiles.title: Letter protesting Matsumoto Jiichirō’s purge
subfiles.about: Urges cancellation of the purge decision against Matsumoto Jiichirō.
subfiles.summary: Derevyanko argues that Matsumoto’s disqualification is unjust, cites his work for outcast emancipation and democracy, and contrasts his treatment with other politicians’ reinstatement.

subfiles.title: Letter from Tokyo on Japan’s recovery and business prospects
subfiles.from: T. Muxo Yamas (signature uncertain in OCR)
subfiles.about: Describes improving conditions in Japan, trade contacts, and a meeting with MacArthur.
subfiles.summary: The writer reports visible recovery, Japanese gratitude for U.S. aid, and hopes for stronger commercial ties.

subfiles.title: Sebald reply on Japanese political realignment
subfiles.about: Clarifies the Political Adviser’s views on conservative, middle, and Communist party groupings.
subfiles.summary: Sebald argues that January’s election strengthened both conservatives and Communists while weakening the middle parties. He favors clearer party alignments, including a consolidated conservative party and a stronger middle grouping formed from liberal Democrats and moderate Socialists. Such a grouping, he says, could give voters dissatisfied with conservatives an alternative to communism.

subfiles.title: Army message on foreign business and investment in Japan
subfiles.from: Department of the Army, Civil Affairs Division
subfiles.about: Requests further review and details before proceeding with proposed foreign investment measures.
subfiles.summary: Seeks investment details and warns that depressed share prices could enable inexpensive foreign control.

subfiles.title: Moscow telegram on Tokyo peace congress
subfiles.about: Relays a Soviet press account of the April Tokyo peace congress.
subfiles.summary: Reports Tass’s account of a peace congress headed by Ikuo Ōyama.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tokyo despatch 242
subfiles.about: Summarizes and evaluates Sebald’s report on the Social Democratic Party’s leftward shift.
subfiles.summary: Green notes greater labor influence, possible resistance to Communist organizing, and reduced prospects for a Democratic-Socialist merger.

subfiles.title: The Social Democratic Party’s Shift to the Left, information copy
subfiles.about: Duplicate filing copy of despatch 242 assessing the Social Democratic Party convention.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the assessment of the party’s stronger left and labor wings, its rejection of an explicitly Marxist platform, and its weakened right wing.
